frontier.hypothesis: v0 is in opposite_needed at insn 686 for a readable reason inside mark_target_live_regs, and once that reason is named the C question becomes concrete.
frontier.mechanism: insn 344 carries REG_DEAD (reg:SI 2 v0), which goes into pending_dead_regs, and reorg.c:2709 flushes pending_dead_regs at every CODE_LABEL. Label 347 IS on the forward walk between insn 344 and target 686, so by the letter of the source v0 should be clear at 686 - yet oppregs has bit 2 set. Either the flush is not reached (a next_insn_no_annul / stop_insn subtlety - note stop_insn is recomputed when the target is a SEQUENCE, reorg.c:2612) or v0 is re-introduced by the second phase that steps forward from TARGET (reorg.c:2732 onward).
frontier.next_probe: Add a DBRDBG print inside mark_target_live_regs' forward loop (insn UID, GET_CODE, and the running current_live_regs word) plus one at the end of the step-forward-from-TARGET phase, rebuild tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1, and re-run tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s10/isolate.py + dumpiso.sh with BB2_DBR_DEBUG=1. Read where bit 2 gets set. If it comes from basic_block_live_at_start[28] and survives the label flush, the C question is what makes label 347 a basic-block head at life_analysis time; if it is re-introduced by the step-forward phase, the C question is about the shape of the fall-through block's first insn (currently the SEQUENCE `bnez s1` with delay `li v0,25`).

frontier.hypothesis: Cluster B (the nop-vs-li v0,1 divergence at emitted slots 45/47) is a delay-slot-fill residual of the SAME kind as the slot-126 one, not an exit-form residual.
frontier.mechanism: s10 proved cluster B does not move under any of the sixteen exit-form assignments, which was the standing explanation for it. A nop at an emitted slot where target has a real instruction is the signature of an unfilled delay slot, and the s10 DBRDBG log already contains every fill decision this function makes.
